title: Motion is not weather. It is geometry.
subtitle: Where you sleep along the length of the ship decides how much of the sea you feel.

points.label: Forward
points.value: The end of the lever. Pitch is felt first here, and hardest, and at anchor too.

points.label: Midship, low
points.value: Nearest the pivot. The least movement on the ship, and the least glamorous address.

points.label: Aft
points.value: Calmer than forward, but you sit over the propellers and feel the vibration.

points.label: High and forward
points.value: The most dramatic view on the ship, and the most motion available for the money.

items.head: Anyone uncertain at sea
items.body: Midship, low, no argument. Stabilisers help underway and do far less at anchor.

items.head: Ocean crossings and shoulder season
items.body: Midship again. Open water in November is not the week to test your inner ear.

items.head: Calm-water itineraries
items.body: Take the aft terrace. Rivers, fjords and the summer Aegean forgive the position entirely.

text: Small ships move more. They also berth where large ones cannot.
sub: That is a real trade, not marketing. You feel more of the sea on a 400-guest ship and you walk off into the town centre instead of queuing for a tender.

text: Decide the itinerary first. Let the water choose the position.
sub: Sheltered coastline and short hops, sit anywhere you like. Open ocean, repositioning legs, or any hesitation about motion — midship and low, and spend the saving on the shore days.

title: Send this to whoever gets queasy.
body: Or tell me the sailing and the month, and I'll tell you whether the water on that route justifies paying for the aft terrace at all.
